fields.after: Your moves can go up 2 more levels (up to 10) and fusions 1 more star (up to ★6).

after.summary: Recalculated for v0.8.25. Starting stats, kits and passive effects are unchanged; opening scores and tiers are unchanged. TM Case supports fusion growth to ★6, which is outside this opening comparison.

fields.before: Bulbasaur is a sensible first choice when repeated small hits are draining your run. Photosynthesis adds regeneration and healing, and Grass hits provide small, capped healing. That rewards keeping attacks connected while you create space. It does not make standing inside a crowd safe.
fields.after: Bulbasaur is a sensible first choice when repeated small hits are draining your run. Synthesis adds regeneration and healing, and Grass hits provide small, capped healing. That rewards keeping attacks connected while you create space. It does not make standing inside a crowd safe.

fields.before: Squirtle gives armor and shield immediately. That is useful when learning how much room a group needs and how far a projectile travels. Charmander’s Blaze increases damage below 40% HP, with a separate Fire bonus. Treat that low-health bonus as help in a bad situation; deliberately sitting at low HP is a rough way to learn an unfamiliar arena.
fields.after: Squirtle gives armor and shield immediately. That is useful when learning how much room a group needs and how far a projectile travels. Charmander’s Sea of Flames increases damage below 40% HP, with a separate Fire bonus. Treat that low-health bonus as help in a bad situation; deliberately sitting at low HP is a rough way to learn an unfamiliar arena.
Synthesis: +1.5 regen and +25% healing. Your Grass attacks heal you a little (0.4% of HP per hit, up to 5 times per second).
Torrent Shell: +15 armor and +20 shield. Below 40% HP, +40% damage.
Sea of Flames: Below 40% HP, +40% damage. +10% Fire damage.

TM Case raises normal moves from level 8 to level 10 and lets a fusion grow from ★5 to ★6. You still only need level 8 on each ingredient to fuse. Do not hold back a useful fusion while waiting for level 10, and do not make finding this Legendary item a condition for a successful first run.

fields.before: Photosynthesis adds +1.5 regen and +25% healing. Grass attacks heal 0.4% of HP per hit, capped at five healing triggers per second. The practical advantage is repeatable recovery while you are already attacking, rather than waiting for a rescue pickup.
fields.after: Synthesis adds +1.5 regen and +25% healing. Grass attacks heal 0.4% of HP per hit, capped at five healing triggers per second. The practical advantage is repeatable recovery while you are already attacking, rather than waiting for a rescue pickup.

A fusion normally stops at ★5. TM Case makes ★6 available and raises the cap on ordinary moves to level 10. If the fusion is already doing the work, another useful star can be a better direction than filling its freed slot with an attack you cannot support. The item changes your growth ceiling, not the level-8 requirement for the ingredient pair. Keep a build that works without it; its Legendary rarity makes it a poor foundation for an opening plan.

Check the patch when copying an older fusion build. Version 0.8.17 fixed fusions ignoring extra projectiles, so an older damage report is a poor baseline for deciding whether that bonus helps now. The pause menu shows damage over the last 15 seconds as well as the total: use the recent window to see what is carrying the current encounter. Different fusion patterns still use projectiles differently, so do not turn one successful example into a rule for every recipe.

fields.before: The Lab is permanent progression. Items and vitamins chosen during a run are a separate system. The figures here apply to v0.8.13; compare the price in your current Lab before committing Stardust.
fields.after: The Lab is permanent progression. Items and vitamins chosen during a run are a separate system. The figures here apply to v0.8.25; compare the price in your current Lab before committing Stardust.

Do not confuse a Lab slot with TM Case. The slot is permanent capacity; TM Case is an item found during a run that raises ordinary moves to level 10 and fusions to ★6. Max Ether raises vitamins to level 12. Neither item buys an extra Lab slot or changes its Stardust price. A slot purchase should make the planned build easier to assemble before either item appears.

Selling either cap item is a real build decision. Without TM Case, ordinary moves above level 8 and fusions above ★5 are trimmed back to those caps. Selling Max Ether removes vitamin levels above 10. Do not sell one just because the displayed level has already been reached; the v0.8.17 fix means those extra levels are no longer kept after the item leaves your inventory.

notes: Fusion class, cooldown, range, power, hit weighting and status fields were not previously published; their addition is an enrichment, not a balance change.
